During the preceding two years, NDWC used commercial AI applications and contractor-supported development services to support educational wargaming, campaign planning, exercise design, faculty development, and AI experimentation. This operational experience demonstrated that an AI- enabled platform can improve the speed, consistency, analytical rigor, and educational value of wargame development and execution. The experience established an enduring requirement for continued access to a secure commercial AI application. f_Work.docx ===== STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) RFID Cabinet The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), requires the acquisition of a Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) storage cabinet integrated with Unique Device Identifier (UDI)-compliant tissue and implant tracking software to support patient safety, regulatory compliance, and efficient inventory management. Tracking tissues, biologics, and implantable medical devices is a federal regulatory requirement under FDA 21 CFR Part 830 (UDI) and is critical to patient safety. VA healthcare facilities face ongoing resource challenges including staff shortages and budget constraints, making it essential to minimize staff time consumed by manual data entry and to maintain precise control over high-value inventory. This acquisition will provide an automated, real-time RFID-based inventory management solution for use in the operating room (OR), Catheterization (Cath) lab, ambulatory surgery center, or any facility location that stores high-value implantable inventory.
